cells.tense: You are holding a chosen direction steady right now, and the whole picture stays visible while you do it.
cells.act: mark the good thing together, out loud
cells.ask: Some good thing is going right. Say it to whoever's standing there — one plain sentence, while it's still warm, before the moment moves past. Let it be shared instead of saved up.
cells.core:
Under load you keep a chosen direction and still take in the entire shape of things — the pattern, who's in it, what it costs. The picture doesn't scatter when the weight lands. You pick your line and hold it, and the people near you can feel the ground stay steady underneath.

Something you all have been carrying is going right, and it is theirs too. Say it while it's still happening, one plain sentence to whoever is standing there — not folded into a recap afterward. Saying a good thing with the people it belongs to is not the prize for keeping on. It is part of why going on is worth anything.
cells.sheetLine: You hold your line and keep the whole picture in view.
cells.place: seeing the whole pattern while standing inside it

cells.tense: You will keep gathering every angle into the defense until there's no room left to see anything at rest.
cells.act: put the problem down and take a walk with nothing to solve
cells.ask: Leave the problem where it sits and go outside with nothing to work out — no deciding, no rehearsing. If it follows you, set it down at the step. The walk is the whole thing.
cells.core:
You catch the whole shape of what might come and get ready for all of it at once — every angle, every version. That's a real skill. Lately the shape is being read so far ahead that you're bracing against things that haven't arrived, and the picture doesn't get to be simply what it is. Taking in everything has become standing ready.

The problem keeps while you're out. Step away and walk with nothing to solve, no decision to reach, nothing held. If it tags along, set it down at the step. A mind that stops comes back clearer, and what you were bracing for isn't any nearer while you're gone.
cells.sheetLine: You're bracing against a shape that hasn't arrived yet.
cells.place: seeing the whole pattern while standing inside it

cells.tense: You were standing in a doorway already closed behind you, reading it from the side you'd left.
cells.act: protect what was won by the ending
cells.ask: Take the thing the last ending actually left you — a truth you don't have to argue, a room that's yours, a habit gone — and hold it in some small form: a note, a chair moved, a line you don't cross.
cells.core:
Something ended, and you haven't quite crossed into what came after. What you take in now is a picture of how things were — accurate, detailed, framed from where you used to stand. The engine that would run on it sits quiet. The reading is happening; it's aimed backward.

An ending leaves something behind worth keeping, and that part doesn't need earning again. Take one thing the last hard ending gave you — a truth you don't have to re-argue, a room that's yours now, a habit you've shed — and give it a small steady form: a note where you'll see it, a chair shifted, a line left uncrossed. Form holds what the change produced.
cells.sheetLine: You read the pattern from the side you already left.
cells.place: seeing the whole pattern while standing inside it

cells.tense: Right now you are reading the whole pattern and crediting it to luck.
cells.act: start building where the false thing fell
cells.ask: On ground where something false already fell, begin a small skilled piece with your hands — a draft, a first message, a sketch. Finish it in a sitting, and tell nobody.
cells.core:
You read what's actually going on — the whole shape, the layers, what holds and what doesn't — and when it comes up you credit it to chance, or to just noticing. Work like that is yours. Your name isn't on it. You've been treating the pattern as something that happens to you, a report you're passing along.

Where something false already fell, the ground is cleared, and nothing's been raised on it. Begin a small skilled piece on that ground with your own hands — a draft, a first message, a sketch — finished before the week turns, nobody told. The clearing wasn't the end of it. It was the floor.
cells.sheetLine: The pattern you're reading is yours, credited to luck.
cells.place: seeing the whole pattern while standing inside it
